name: Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd
title: Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd - 530305 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Piccadily Q1 FY27 revenue rose 8.1% to Rs 270 crore (distillery +26.3%), while branded alco-bev grew 47.3% to Rs 82.3 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose to about Rs 270.5 crore and EBITDA to Rs 47.2 crore, with margin up 30 bps to 18.5%. PAT grew 15.4% to about Rs 22 crore and EPS to Rs 2.21. Premium, super premium and luxury brands reached 43.5% of distillery revenue versus 37.8% a year earlier. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 60% company revenue growth, 60-70% branded alco-bev growth and a 23-24% EBITDA margin, with most revenue expected in H2. Chhattisgarh distillery contributed only about Rs 5 crore from roughly 15 days of production.

financial_highlights.change: +8.1% YoY as stated in prepared remarks (CFO said 18.1%)

financial_highlights.metric: Branded alco-bev (premium, super premium, luxury) revenue
Share of branded in distillery revenue

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 87 lakh last quarter; mainly FX gain and scrap sale

segments.name: Distillery (total)
segments.commentary: Rs 205.7 crore revenue, 76% of total revenue (71% a year earlier). Segment margin fell YoY, which management attributed to cost pressure on grain and fuel and to mix shift toward lower-margin Whistler.

segments.name: Branded alco-bev (IMFL)
segments.commentary: Rs 82.3 crore, +47.3% YoY. Indri grew high double digits; Whistler grew more than 60% in the quarter; Camikara entered CSD and began contributing.

segments.name: Chhattisgarh distillery
segments.commentary: Commissioned, with about 15 days of production in Q1 and roughly Rs 5 crore revenue. Capacity is 210 KLPD; utilisation targeted at about 50% by year-end.

segments.name: Sugar division
segments.commentary: Demerger scheme filed with exchanges on 28 April 2026; process ongoing. Management expects the hive-off by year-end; company-level margin guidance includes sugar.

guidance_outlook: Branded alco-bev revenue to grow about 60-70% in FY27; H2 expected to contribute about 60-65% of annual branded revenue.
Company-level revenue growth target of about 60% YoY for FY27.
Company-level EBITDA margin of 23-24% for FY27 (includes sugar); management said full-year margin should be similar to or slightly better than FY26's 23%.
Chhattisgarh revenue guidance of Rs 300-400 crore for FY27 reiterated; Indri incremental sales guidance of Rs 250-300 crore reiterated.
Barrel inventory expected at 1.15-1.20 lakh barrels by March 2027, above the 1 lakh target.
No large capex planned for FY27 beyond ordinary-course upgrades; company does not plan to increase debt this year.
capex_capacity: Chhattisgarh distillery commissioned; about 15 days of production in Q1 and first revenue in June 2026. Capacity 210 KLPD; utilisation targeted at about 50% by March 2027.
Indri distillery expansion running at about 60% utilisation.
Malt capacity added last year (30 KL) running at about 80%.
Barrel inventory of 87,000 filled barrels (200-500 litre sizes); about 60-70 lakh litres added each year.
Management stated the company is not planning large capex this year; most heavy capex is complete.
demand_pricing: Indri growing 18-20% YoY, which management described as the only single malt growing at that pace; global single malts are growing 2-3%.
Whistler grew almost 100% last year and more than 60% this quarter; Camikara and Cashmir expected to grow in triple digits this year from a small base.
Management says it will not disclose individual brand margins and speaks only at portfolio level.
Ethanol margin about 10%; country liquor margin about 15-18%; management said branded margins are not under pressure, while distillery ex-branded faces price pressure from grain and fuel costs.
Receivables: branded receivables about Rs 170 crore (incl. excise), receivable days about 100 versus higher in March after a Rs 100 crore March sales spike.
Exports about 25% of sales; management targets a long-term 70% export / 30% domestic mix; North America is the largest export market; exports to 31 countries.
A court order in Chennai halted ethanol plants; management expects orders to resume in Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 47.3% branded growth and what is the Chhattisgarh contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Indri grew high double digits, Whistler more than 60%, and Camikara began contributing via CSD. Chhattisgarh contributed about Rs 5 crore from roughly 15 days of production.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin rise only 30 bps and how are costs trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to mix, with Indri the highest-margin product. Cost pressure from grain and fuel hit the distillery segment. Employee, distribution and brand investment costs rose ahead of H2 revenue, and management expects margins to recover as revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough aged malt to support Indri growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. The company holds 87,000 filled barrels, which management called the largest in India, and sees no supply constraint for 18-20% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indri scale ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to reach top-five single malt volumes of about 0.5 million cases in 4-5 years, implying about Rs 1,200 crore Indri revenue at current prices. Current capacity supports about 8-8.5 lakh cases if all malt went to Indri.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chhattisgarh ethanol exposure a guidance risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 300-400 crore guidance is intact and that ethanol is a stopgap; the company plans branded products from Chhattisgarh. It declined to split ethanol and alco-bev revenue until Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will debt fall and what is the working capital position?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 crore of debt was repaid in Q1. Management plans no net debt increase this year, with larger reductions from FY28 after investment in liquid and barrels. Receivable days fell to about 100.

risks_watch: Chennai court order halting ethanol plants: management expects orders to resume in Q2 and Q3; Rs 300-400 crore Chhattisgarh guidance depends on the ethanol/alco-bev mix, which management has not split until Q3.

Margin trajectory: distillery segment margin fell YoY on grain and fuel costs and Whistler mix; employee, distribution and brand costs rose ahead of H2, so the 23-24% company EBITDA margin needs H2 revenue to land.

Indri growth of 18-20% versus the 60-70% branded target: the gap must come from Whistler, Camikara, Cashmir and new launches, with some launches in Q2 and Q3 and no split of brand-level numbers disclosed.
Sugar division demerger (scheme filed 28 April 2026) expected to be completed by year-end; company-level margin guidance includes sugar, so the hive-off affects reported comparisons.
Receivables: branded receivables about Rs 170 crore including excise, with receivable days around 100; watch collection after the March sales spike and the H2 seasonal build.
Chhattisgarh ramp: about 15 days of production in Q1, targeted about 50% utilisation by March 2027, and a 210 KLPD capacity base.
key_quotes: We remain confident in our ability to deliver a company-level EBITDA margin in the range of 23% to 24% for FY27, while continuing to invest behind our brands, new product launches, distribution capabilities, and international expansion.

So we see that the margin should not contract because all the other IMFL brands if we are to take the sugar unit out of the mix our distillery division margins are much higher than the 23, 24 that we are talking about.
So we ultimately want to have 70% export and 30% domestic. But that goal will is a few years away.
So that is where the EBITDA margins will come back to the last year or slightly better as we increase, two things will happen.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year branded growth (60-70%), company revenue growth (about 60%) and the 23-24% EBITDA margin, and firm that the Chhattisgarh guidance is intact. Noticeably cautious and evasive on brand-level margins, volumes, the ethanol/alco-bev split at Chhattisgarh and ethanol policy, repeatedly declining to give numbers and deferring details to Q3.

adds.what: 210 KLPD Chhattisgarh distillery (commissioned; ~15 days production in Q1)

growth.why: Management reiterated ~60% FY27 company revenue growth and 60-70% branded growth, backed by the commissioned 210 KLPD Chhattisgarh distillery (Rs 300-400 crore FY27 guide) and Indri incremental sales of Rs 250-300 crore, but no new order book or contracted volumes were quantified and the Chennai ethanol halt adds risk.
